newsitem.title: USA: Sen Moynihan reoffers controversial stadiums bill.
newsitem.headline: Sen Moynihan reoffers controversial stadiums bill.

text.p: U.S. Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan, (D-NY), reintroduced a measure Tuesday to to bar use of tax-exempt bonds for professional sports stadiums.
Moynihan also reoffered a bill that would eliminate a federal curb on bond issuance that he said denies tax-exempt financing to large, private research institutions.
That curb sets a $150 million cap on the amount of tax-exempt bonds that nonhospital 501(c)(3) organizations can have outstanding.

Moynihan originally introduced the stadiums bill last year with a June 14, 1996 effective date. But, he agreed to delay that date when bond dealers and issuers said the deadline had a chilling effect on some major stadium financings and the market for stadium bonds.
The senator's new stadium bill would take effect when the Senate Finance Committee or House Ways and Means Committee votes on the measure.
The stadiums bill also would exempt bonds issued before the effective date that are refunded on a current basis.
The new bill does not include carve outs for very small stadiums or charitable uses of facilities, which were considered by Moynihan staff.
An aide said, however, that the senator is still "open to comment regarding specifics on the bill."
